edition.fact: Edition 44. Wednesday 18 November 2026. This edition runs 4,452 words. Nvidia's first post-Huang quarter beat across the board - $115.8 billion of revenue, up 103% against the $109.1 billion expected, and a $130 billion guide against the $125.1 billion expected; the stock rose about 5% after hours. Huang offered to return; the board said it does not intend to ask. Anthropic prices tonight, with CNBC's sources pointing above the range; Mumbai set nine-month highs on record foreign buying. The long read: TSMC - the company that only makes other people's chips.
edition.intro: The 5-minute lead route is first; sections carry the detail. The long read: the chips behind Nvidia's record quarter came from one firm in Hsinchu - and Morris Chang was twice sidelined and past fifty when he invented the pure-play foundry. TSMC, the AI trade's quiet landlord.

blocks.html: Nvidia answered. The first quarter of the post-Huang era came in at $115.8 billion of revenue - up 103% on the year and well above the $109.1 billion analysts expected - with data center at $107.6 billion, up 110%, and a fourth-quarter guide of $130 billion, give or take 3%, against the $125.1 billion expected (the company's release; LSEG's estimates via CNBC). It was Colette Kress's first print as interim CEO and CFO, and the market's verdict was immediate: the stock, down 24% in November going in, rose about 5% in extended trading (the after-hours read). The guide's fine print: it includes an extra week in the quarter, assumes no China data-center compute revenue, and guides gross margin down to 71-72%.

The leadership file moved twice on the same evening. Jensen Huang issued his first statement since resigning: "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO" (CNBC's live report). Board chair Harvey C. Jones closed that door on the call itself: the board "does not intend" to reinstate Huang, having unanimously accepted his resignation - after what the company now describes as disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with its code of conduct (Politico's report; TechCrunch's report). Those are the company's words, reported as such; this paper adds nothing to them.

Wall Street had sold the rumor. Tuesday was the S&P 500's fourth straight loss - down 1.03% to 7,340.53, its lowest close since July - with the Dow off 848.75 points to 50,759.42 and the Nasdaq down 0.74% to 24,328.38; all eleven sectors fell (the closing wire). Salesforce sank 9% as enterprise software slid ahead of Anthropic's debut (the software selloff). Then the print landed and futures turned: S&P 500 futures up about 0.7-0.8%, Nasdaq 100 futures up about 1.4-1.6% overnight (the futures board). Separately, the NSA confirmed an outage of an internal classified network after what it called scheduled maintenance; officials said there was no indication of an attack (the AP's report).

Mumbai, meanwhile, set records. The Sensex rose 427.40 points to 82,532.19 and the Nifty 96.30 to 25,387.40 - both at nine-month highs, having recovered every point lost since 27 February (the BusinessLine close). The Nifty Bank hit a record 62,422 intraday; FIIs bought a twelfth straight session - a provisional Rs 4,195.38 crore - taking November's foreign inflows past $9.5 billion, a record month (the flow tally). The rupee joined in: 93.48 to the dollar, its strongest close in seven months (the currency report). Falling crude did the lifting for autos, paints and airlines.

Anthropic's order books closed at 4 PM in New York on Tuesday, and the offering is likely to price above its $70-78 range, CNBC reports, citing people familiar - an expectation, not an outcome (the report). Pricing is tonight, New York time; the first trade is Thursday as ANT. The tape it prices into: a software sector it has already marked down, and an AI trade that Nvidia just steadied. The day's third gate is the Fed: minutes of the October meeting land today, with futures pricing a December rate rise as near-certain, per CME FedWatch (the rates board).

The BIS compute rule is still not law. Two days after its release, the Federal Register carries no publication entry for RIN 0694-AK50 - checked again this morning - so every clock in the rule (the effective date, the sixty-day comments, the ninety-day runway) has yet to start (the Register; the rule text). Until the entry exists, the rule remains released, not operative.

Overnight markers, as of about 6 AM IST: Brent $93.14; the dollar index at 103.49; gold at $3,841.60, down 0.58%; the US ten-year at 5.115% (CNBC's quote boards); the VIX closed Tuesday at 25.46, up 11.13%; GIFT Nifty at 25,358.50, up 0.03%, pointing to a flat open near 25,395 - an indication, not an open (the pre-market screen). Tokyo opened higher on the Nvidia print - the Nikkei up about 147 points at the open, gains widening past 400 within minutes (the Tokyo open).

The long read: the company that only makes other people's chips. The chips behind Nvidia's record quarter came from one firm in Hsinchu - and Morris Chang was twice sidelined and past fifty when he invented its model. TSMC, the pure-play foundry, as the AI trade's quiet landlord (read it here). The route ends. The detail begins.

The print, in full. Revenue of $115.8 billion - up 103% year on year, up 20% on the quarter - with data center at $107.6 billion, up 110% year on year; GAAP gross margin of 74.8%; GAAP earnings of $2.70 a share; net income of $65.3 billion, up 105% (the release). Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are shipping - the fastest ramp in the company's history, it says - with CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Azure, OCI and Nebius among the first customers. The Hugging Face acquisition remains on track. Four customers made up 47% of the quarter's sales - the concentration number to carry into the Concept section below. Kress told the call that Anthropic's annualized revenue reached $81 billion at the end of October, and raised the company's FY28 growth outlook to 75% from 70% - the company's outlook, in its own framing.

What the beat is made of. The $130 billion guide is a real beat - $125.1 billion was the consensus - but it is a constructed one, and the construction is disclosed: the quarter carries an extra week, and the number assumes zero China data-center compute revenue (the release). Gross margin is guided down to 71-72% from 74.8% - the cost of the Rubin ramp. And the shareholder returns keep pace: $28.1 billion went out in buybacks and dividends in the quarter, with $227.3 billion of authorization remaining. The stock's +5% after-hours answer followed a 24% November slide - six straight weekly drops, the longest such run since 2012 (CNBC's live report).

The leadership exchange, on the record. Huang's statement Tuesday was his first since the resignation, and it offered a return: "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO" (the statement as reported). Jones, on the call, said the board unanimously accepted the resignation and does not intend to reinstate him - and the company's account of the resignation itself has now gained one official sentence: it followed disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with Nvidia's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms (Politico; TechCrunch). That sentence is the whole of what the company has said on the subject. A search for a permanent chief continues.

The day the print landed into. Tuesday's regular session was a selloff: the S&P 500's fourth straight loss and lowest close since July, every sector red, financials the worst at -1.87% (the closing wire). The AI complex's own anxiety showed in software, where Salesforce's 9% fall led the S&P's decliners as Anthropic's IPO approached - investors are repricing the application layer the new models aim at (the software read). Nvidia closed the regular session at $155.46, down 0.44%, before the numbers changed the conversation (the session recap). One session of futures is not a recovery; it is a repricing of the print.

Mumbai's record day, in full. The Nifty's close at 25,387.40 completes the recovery from 27 February - the day the US-Iran war losses began - with 22 constituents now above their levels of that date; Eternal, Kotak Mahindra Bank and ICICI Bank touched 52-week highs (the session's anatomy). Banks did the heavy lifting - the Nifty Bank's record 62,422 intraday, closing up 697 points - while cheaper crude lifted Eicher, M&M, Asian Paints and InterGlobe, and Reliance rose 2% to a six-month high as the index's biggest contributor. The tell that it was a large-cap day: the advance-decline ratio was flat at 1:1, and small-caps slipped 0.2%. UPL faded from its high on reports its restructuring may be revised; KEI fell 4% on price-cut reports; Ashok Leyland spiked, then closed 8% below its day's high; Laurus Labs gained over 5% after management ruled out further stake sales.

The debut that prices tonight. Anthropic's books closed Tuesday afternoon in New York, with the offering likely to price above the $70-78 range, per CNBC's sourcing - reported here as an expectation, not a result (the report). The third amended filing landed the same day (the S-1/A-3). Nine-month revenue of $33.24 billion, up roughly twelvefold, against a nine-month net loss of $104 billion - most of it the fair-value accounting of convertible notes. The concurrent $26 billion supplier placement closes immediately after the offering. First trade: Thursday, as ANT.

Tuesday's marks, then this morning's markers. Mumbai: Sensex 82,532.19, up 427.40 (0.52%); Nifty 25,387.40, up 96.30 (0.38%) - both nine-month highs (the close). New York: S&P 500 7,340.53, down 1.03%; Nasdaq 24,328.38, down 0.74%; Dow 50,759.42, down 1.64%; VIX 25.46, up 11.13% (the wire; the board). This morning, as of about 6 AM IST: S&P 500 futures up 0.8% at 7,418.25 and Nasdaq 100 futures up 1.6% at 27,497.75 (the futures report, timestamped 5:22 AM IST); Brent $93.14; gold $3,841.60, down 0.58%; the dollar index 103.49; the US ten-year at 5.115% (CNBC's quote boards); GIFT Nifty at 25,358.50, up 0.03% - a flat indication, not an open (the pre-market screen). Tokyo opened up 147 points at 59,007.40 and widened gains past 400 early (the open). The day's schedule: the Fed's October minutes this evening; Anthropic prices tonight New York time.

The largest AI listing ever attempted gets its price tonight. Anthropic's 825 million Class A shares at $70 to $78 price Wednesday evening in New York - the third amended filing is in, the books are closed, and CNBC's sources say the price is likely to land above the range; treat that as reported expectation until the print (the filing; the pricing report). The valuation sought runs to roughly $1.4 trillion, and the sector it lands in has already been repriced: Salesforce, ServiceNow, Workday and Adobe all fell Tuesday as investors weighed what the new models do to the application layer (the software slide). In Mumbai, Urban Company opened a Rs 2,500-crore QIP with a floor of Rs 161.03 per share - up to a 5% discount permitted - and Rediff filed updated IPO papers (the startup wire).

blocks.html: Realty carried the day: Oberoi, Godrej Properties and Prestige all gained more than 2.4%, with Adani Enterprises the board's leader at +3.12% (the session report). The two extremes are both reversals: Ashok Leyland closed at Rs 160.65, down 4.26% - and 8% below its own day's high - giving back Monday's post-print gain, while Tata Communications shed 2.82% after leading Monday's board. Tata Motors PV steadied at Rs 259.55, down 1.01% after Monday's 8.64% verdict. Carried closes for the ledger: ONGC Rs 223.60, Tata Steel Rs 181.55, SAIL Rs 171.20, ITC Rs 293.00.

Wednesday's board is thin - a small-cap day (the week's calendar). Ansal Properties, BLS Polymers and GVP Infotech feature in the results lane; Aye Finance has an NCD raise; Bonlon Industries prices its rights issue. Thursday is busier: Muthoot Microfin reports, and Natco Pharma's dividend record date arrives. Friday carries the twin record dates for Ashok Leyland's Re 1 interim and Oil India's dividend - both names on today's movers board, for different reasons.

What after-hours actually tells you. Nvidia fell 0.44% in Tuesday's regular session, reported at 1:20 PM Pacific, and rose about 5% in extended trading - three prices for one stock in one day, and only the first is the deep market (the session recap; the extended session). The mechanics matter: after-hours trading runs on thin volume, wide spreads and retail-heavy flow, so an extended-session move is a first vote, not a verdict - the regular open re-prices it with full participation. The useful habit is to treat the overnight number as information about direction and surprise, not about level: it tells you the print beat or missed the whisper, not where the stock will trade at the close. The same logic applies to this morning's GIFT Nifty line, to futures up on the Nvidia print, and to Anthropic's price tonight: indications are inputs, not outcomes. The paper labels each one as-of, and the open decides.

Tuesday's cheques, largest first (the daily roundup). Dreamteam raised $53 million from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest - founded in 2025 by three ex-Freshworks executives (Anand Venkatraman, Ramesh Parthasarathy, Senthil Kanthaswamy), it is building an AI-first CRM, with InVideo and Plex as customers. CountAI took a Rs 10-crore seed from Equirus InnovateX for its Knit-I fabric-defect cameras - KPR and Indorama are customers. finny.club raised Rs 5.3 crore in an angel round that included Juspay's Ramanathan RV - it is SEBI-registered. JohnAIC raised $1.9 million pre-seed from Crane Venture Partners for on-premise AI servers, and Lemonpeel $1 million pre-seed from Shastra VC for AI video. In the listed lane, Urban Company opened its Rs 2,500-crore QIP (floor Rs 161.03), and Rediff filed updated IPO papers.

Today's startup idea: the audit ledger for agentic commerce. The prompt is this week's direction of travel - Microsoft shipping agent models, TSMC's CEO crediting "agentic AI" for demand, and Anthropic about to list (the Ignite lineup). As companies let AI agents browse, negotiate and pay, the question nobody owns yet is bookkeeping: what did the agent see, what did it decide, what did it spend, and who proves it in a dispute? The idea, with its limits stated: a neutral transaction ledger for agent actions - signed records of prompts, prices and payments that finance and legal teams can audit - sold per logged transaction. The limits: there is no settled standard for agent identity or consent, liability frameworks are unwritten, and the payment networks and model providers may bundle this before a startup can price it - in which case the honest pivot is the dispute-evidence layer, where independence is the product. What would make it wrong: agents staying read-only for another year.

Two price lists, one direction. OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: Astra posts a new high on the Agents' Last Exam - 5.2 points above GPT-6 Astra at less than a third of the cost, and 5.5 above Claude Fable 5.2 at 5% of the cost - with API pricing of $8 per million input tokens ($0.40 cached) and $40 per million output, 20% below its predecessor; on the Harvey legal benchmark it claims more than double Fable 5.2's pass rate at about a sixth of the cost (the release). Microsoft used Ignite to ship seven models of its own - MAI Cyber 2 Flash, Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Image 2.7, Realtime 1, Transcribe 2 for Dragon Copilot, and Decision 1.1 - and put its Maia 200 accelerator into production at a claimed 1.7x tokens per watt (the Ignite announcements). The frame the week has built: the model layer keeps cutting prices and shipping capability, while the silicon layer underneath prints records. Both cannot be a bubble at once - and both claims are now on the tape.

The browser is becoming the server. Simon Willison has rewritten Datasette Lite so the full Datasette Python application - server, database engine, plugins - runs inside a browser tab on WebAssembly, via service workers and Pyodide, with no install and no backend (his write-up). The builder's lesson is not the demo; it is the architecture. A URL can now carry the entire environment: which Datasette version, which plugins from PyPI, which data files - so a bug report or a data demo becomes a link, not a setup guide. When you build a tool, ask what its "lite" version would be: the whole product, minus the server, shipped as a link. The constraint that makes it work is also the lesson: browsers are sandboxed, so state lives with the user and nothing phones home - privacy as a deployment model. The limits are real too: WASM payloads are heavy, large datasets strain a tab, and persistence is yours to arrange.

Run a database in a browser tab. Open lite.datasette.io and point it at any public CSV, JSON or SQLite file - the tool loads it client-side and gives you a full queryable, filterable interface (the author's examples). Free, on the web, no login; the demo link on the write-up loads a mapping plugin and a sample dataset if you want the guided version. Try it with a file you already know - a portfolio export, a spending CSV - and notice how much more you see in a table you can filter than in the same rows in a spreadsheet. The limits: everything runs in your tab, so very large files will strain it; your data never leaves your machine, which is the point but also means there is nothing to come back to once you close it; and sharing means sending someone the crafted URL, data file included.

Then, a reading habit for tonight: the owning document. When Anthropic prices, the recap will be everywhere - read the filing first. The SEC's full-text search (efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22Anthropic%22 - or the EDGAR full-text page at sec.gov) is free, on the web, no login. Search the company, open the S-1/A, and read the risk factors and the concurrent placement before you read anyone's summary of them (the current amendment). The limits: EDGAR is a document store, not an explainer - it gives you what the company filed, in the company's words, with no one to translate the accounting. That is also its value: every claim in tomorrow's coverage traces back to what you can read tonight.

Four customers made 47% of Nvidia's $115.8 billion quarter - that single line, from Tuesday's release, is a customer-concentration disclosure, and it is one of the most load-bearing numbers in any filing (the release). The concept: US disclosure rules make a company name any customer above 10% of revenue, and the resulting figure measures how much of the business depends on how few decisions. Concentration is not automatically fragility - those four are presumably the largest AI build-outs on earth, and their orders are the boom - but it converts four companies' budgets into one company's risk factor. Read it as a dependency map: when a handful of buyers fund the whole build-out, their capex guidance is the supplier's revenue forecast. The habit transfers directly to Indian filings, where the same dependency hides in segment notes: find the line that says how much of revenue the top customers carry, and you have found the company's real sensitivity.

groups.heading: Term of the day: book building

blocks.html: When CNBC reports that Anthropic's "order books closed" at 4 PM, the term is book building: the process by which an issuer's banks collect bids from institutions - how many shares, at what price - before setting the final offer price (the report). The book is the tally of those bids; closing it ends the auction; pricing is the judgment that follows. An oversubscribed book is why an offering can price above its range: more demand than shares at the top end lets the banks move the clearing price up. The same mechanism runs in Mumbai - Urban Company's Rs 2,500-crore QIP, opened Tuesday with a Rs 161.03 floor, is a book-built offer to institutions under SEBI's rules (the QIP report). Watch for it tonight in the Anthropic print: the price, the multiple of the range, and what the book said.

Tuesday's session is scored. No stop touched, no target taken - but Infosys's floor had its closest call: the day's low of Rs 1,126.00 came within six points of the 1,120 close-based floor, and the close at Rs 1,130.00 keeps the thesis alive by its own rule. Every price below is a BSE official close from Tuesday's tape. The desk's rule stands: every published setup stays on the board until it resolves by its own rules.

blocks.html: A week of scenarios met a print. Since Monday, the AI trade had been priced as contingency: the Fed chairman's downside scenario, target cuts ahead of the numbers, six straight weekly losses in the stock itself, and software names sold against a competitor's listing. Tuesday night replaced contingency with arithmetic - $115.8 billion of revenue, a $130 billion guide, margins guided down on purpose - and the after-hours vote reversed the day's entire mood in minutes. The honest reading keeps both facts: the print was strong, and one print does not retire the scenario it answered. The same discipline applies to the evening's other exchange. Huang said he would be honored to return; the board said it does not intend to ask. Both statements now sit on the record, in the principals' own words - and the record, not the rumor, is where this story lives until the search for a permanent chief ends. Price the stated stage, not the headline's certainty: released is not operative, a guide is not a quarter, and a pricing tonight is not a debut Thursday.

The leadership file. Cause chain: Huang's resignation, now officially characterized as following disclosure of conduct inconsistent with the code of conduct; his first statement Tuesday offering to return; Jones's on-call answer that the board does not intend to reinstate him; Kress interim CEO and CFO, one strong print delivered. What settles it: the appointment of a permanent chief. Watch: any search announcement, and whether the board's position holds under shareholder pressure.

The debut file. Cause chain: three amended filings; books closed Tuesday 4 PM New York; likely above-range pricing per CNBC's sourcing; the $26 billion supplier placement closing after; first trade Thursday as ANT. What settles it: tonight's price, then Thursday's first print. Watch: New York tonight and the opening cross.

The compute-rule file. Cause chain: released Monday as RIN 0694-AK50; no Federal Register entry as of Wednesday morning; every clock in the rule still waiting on publication. What settles it: the Register entry - its date starts every clock. Watch: federalregister.gov, and the comment file once it opens.

items: Sources read for this edition: Nvidia's own results release and quarterly call coverage; CNBC's live earnings blog for the Huang statement and the Jones exchange, cross-checked against Politico and TechCrunch; the closing market wire and Reuters' market wrap (which settled a conflicting oil figure from another wrap - Brent rose Tuesday; the wrong figure was discarded); the NSA outage confirmed at the agency's own statement and the AP; CNBC's Anthropic pricing report, kept as attributed expectation; the S-1/A-3 filing; the Hindu BusinessLine and CNBCTV18 for the Mumbai close and flows; Moneycontrol for the rupee; a Federal Register API check this morning - no publication entry for RIN 0694-AK50; OpenAI's and Microsoft's own announcements; StartupTalky's funding roundup; Simon Willison's Datasette Lite write-up; BSE's official bhavcopy for Indian prices; and the GIFT pre-market screen, labeled as-of.

Framing calls this edition: the company's outlook (the FY28 growth raise, the Q4 guide) is reported as the company's own framing, not as settled outcome; Anthropic's above-range pricing is an attributed expectation, not a result; the resignation is described only in the words the company and the principals have used - no allegations beyond the board's stated sentence; an aggregator's claims of fresh PMI and tax data were checked and dropped as stale; the GIFT Nifty and futures lines are as-of indications, not opens.
Prices are BSE official closes or the named settlement prints; provisional flow figures are labeled provisional. Nothing here is investment advice.
